content: 1. L.E. Kamungoma and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial in Zambia to evaluate the use of HIV self-testing among female sex workers. The study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2017. 2. A.T. Choko and colleagues investigated the effectiveness of HIV self-testing, both alone and in combination with additional interventions such as financial incentives and linkage to care, among male partners of antenatal care attendees in Malawi. This adaptive multi-arm, multi-stage cluster-randomized trial was published in PLoS Medicine in 2019. 3. A.T. Choko and colleagues conducted a pragmatic cluster-randomized trial in Malawi to assess the uptake, yield, and accuracy of secondary distribution of HIV self-test kits to partners of antenatal and index HIV-positive patients. The findings were presented at the 14th International AIDS Impact Conference in London in 2019. 4. A cluster-randomized trial in Malawi demonstrated that facility-based HIV self-testing for outpatients significantly increased HIV testing rates. This study was presented at the 22nd International AIDS Conference in Amsterdam in 2018. 5. K. Hatzold and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Zimbabwe to evaluate innovative demand-creation strategies aimed at increasing voluntary medical male circumcision (VMMC) uptake. The findings were shared through personal communication in 2019. 6. A community-based cluster-randomized trial in rural Malawi demonstrated that HIV self-testing increased knowledge of HIV status and demand for antiretroviral therapy. The results were presented at the 22nd International AIDS Conference in Amsterdam in 2018. 7. P.P. Indravudh and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in rural Malawi to assess the impact of community-led delivery of HIV self-testing targeting adolescents and men. The findings were presented at the IAS Conference in Mexico in 2019. 8. P. MacPherson and colleagues evaluated the effect of optional home initiation of HIV care following self-testing on antiretroviral therapy initiation among adults in Malawi. This randomized clinical trial was published in JAMA in 2014. 9. C. Mulubwa and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Zambia to assess the community-based distribution of oral HIV self-testing kits within four HPTN 071 (PopART) intervention communities. The study was published in The Lancet in 2019. 10. B.E. Nichols and colleagues analyzed the cost and impact of community-based, assisted HIV self-testing among youth in Zambia. The findings were presented at the Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in Seattle in 2019. 11. K. Ortblad and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized controlled health systems trial in Uganda to compare direct provision versus facility collection of HIV self-tests among female sex workers. The study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2017. 12. M. Shahmanesh and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized controlled trial in rural KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa, to evaluate the effect of peer-delivered HIV self-screening on linkage to HIV prevention. Interim analysis results were presented at the 14th International AIDS Impact Conference in London in 2019. 13. E. Sibanda and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Zimbabwe to evaluate linkage to care after HIV self-testing. The findings were presented at the 25th Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections in Boston in 2018. 14. W. Tang and colleagues conducted a closed cohort stepped wedge cluster-randomized controlled trial in China to assess the use of crowdsourcing to expand HIV testing among men who have sex with men. The study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2018. 15. D. Tsamwa and colleagues conducted a cluster-randomized trial in Zambia to evaluate whether community distribution of HIV self-test kits increases population-level HIV testing uptake. The findings were presented at the HIV Research for Prevention Conference in 2018. 16. W. Chang and colleagues conducted a randomized clinical trial in Zimbabwe to assess the effect of pricing, distribution strategies, and marketing on demand for HIV self-testing. The study was published in JAMA Network Open in 2019. 17. A.T. Choko and colleagues conducted a pilot trial in Uganda to evaluate the peer-based distribution of HIV self-test kits among fishermen. The study was published in PLoS One in 2018. 18. A.T. Choko and colleagues conducted a community-based prospective study in Malawi to evaluate the uptake, accuracy, safety, and linkage to care over two years of promoting annual HIV self-testing. The study was published in PLoS Medicine in 2015. 19. D.F. Conserve and colleagues conducted formative research in Tanzania to develop the Tanzania HIV self-testing education and promotion (STEP) project targeting men. The study was published in PLoS One in 2018. 20. R.J. Dacombe and colleagues conducted a qualitative study in Malawi, Zambia, and Zimbabwe to explore the regulation of HIV self-testing with key stakeholders. The findings were published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2019. 21. C.A. Gaydos and colleagues evaluated the feasibility of patients performing their own rapid HIV tests in emergency departments. The study was published in Annals of Emergency Medicine in 2011. 22. T. Greacen and colleagues explored the perspectives of pharmacists in France on dispensing HIV self-tests. The findings were presented at the International AIDS Conference in 2018. 23. S.A. Lippman and colleagues evaluated the acceptability and feasibility of HIV self-testing among transgender women in San Francisco. The study was published in AIDS and Behavior in 2016. 24. J.K.B. Matovu and colleagues conducted a study in Uganda to explore perceptions, delivery strategies, and post-test experiences of HIV self-testing among pregnant women and their male partners. The study was published in Global Health Action in 2018. 25. S. Mavedzenge and colleagues evaluated the feasibility of HIV self-test programming among female sex workers in Zimbabwe. The findings were presented at the 9th IAS Conference on HIV Science in 2017.
